assumptions: THIS INCREMENT CHANGES NO DECISION AND NO CODE. Three of this package's six blockers are spent and one had a conclusion that went false; two are untouched because they are still true.
SPENT: the blocker saying RFC-2026-019 was Proposed and awaiting disposition. That record was disposed on 2026-09-06; read its status line for the wording rather than this file.

SPENT, AND THIS ONE IS THE INTERESTING REMOVAL. The blocker said RFC-2026-018's status line still recorded only that it was disposed, while the record had been superseded -- and it called that "the most dangerous shape a record can have here", a record that must not be implemented reading as one that may. That line now carries the supersession explicitly, dated 2026-09-06, along with the fact that it was NEVER IN EFFECT and why. The dangerous shape is gone, so the blocker that named it goes with it.

SPENT: the blocker saying the three lint rules RFC-2026-019 §5 names are not written. All three are, and each was checked against the file rather than assumed -- authenticator's non-membership at scripts/db/run.mjs:307, the app_command owner refusal at :632, and the SECURITY DEFINER search_path plus recorded owner at :1003 against catalog-snapshot.json's security_definer_functions list.

REWRITTEN, NOT REMOVED: "Nothing in the tree implements the decision, deliberately." That is now false in its main clause and still true in a part. §5 names FOUR rules and says plainly that the fourth cannot be written before a command function exists; three are written and no command function exists. So the blocker keeps the fourth and drops the claim that nothing is implemented.

TWO ARE UNCHANGED BECAUSE THEY ARE STILL TRUE, and one was verified rather than assumed: the countersignature in evidence/WP-0A-DB-00/a1-countersignature-role-topology.md is against RFC-2026-016 and RFC-2026-017, not this record, and no evidence file in the tree is a review of RFC-2026-019. The G0 blocker carries no false tail here, unlike its siblings in -006, -007 and -008, so it is left exactly as written.
amends_without_owning IS EMPTIED. Four paths from the earlier increment, none touched here.

STATUS IS DELIBERATELY NOT MOVED: this package stays in_progress. An Author may move work only as far as in_review, and moving it would be a claim about completeness rather than the correction of false sentences. It is worth saying for THIS package in particular, because half its blockers just went away and that could easily be read as the package being finished.

security_privacy_cost_impact: None to the code. One security-relevant statement did change meaning: the manifest no longer says the three RFC-2026-019 §5 lint rules are unwritten, because they are written and they are the assertions that keep `authenticator` out of the service roles and keep app_command from owning a table. A reader who believed the old blocker would have thought those negatives were unasserted.
known_limitations: NOTHING PREVENTS THE NEXT STALE SENTENCE. A blocker list is prose and no lint reads English.

THE THREE LINT RULES ARE CITED BY LINE NUMBER, WHICH IS THE SAME KIND OF CLAIM THIS REPOSITORY HAS WATCHED GO STALE. A line number moves on the next edit to that file. They are cited by line AND by what the rule asserts, so a reader whose line number is wrong can still find the rule; the pairing is the mitigation and it is not a guarantee.
HALF THIS PACKAGE'S BLOCKERS WENT AWAY IN ONE INCREMENT, and that is the shape most likely to be misread as completion. The status is unchanged and the handoff says so twice.
open_risks_or_blockers: Three blockers remain OPEN and are listed in the manifest. This increment closes none of them: it removes ones that were already discharged elsewhere.
rollback_or_forward_fix: ROLLBACK: revert this commit. The manifest returns to six blockers, three describing states that no longer hold and one claiming nothing in the tree implements a decision that is implemented three ways.
recommended_next_work_packages: A review of RFC-2026-019 by the co-owner of the question it answers. That blocker is the one this increment could not discharge and it is the oldest open item on this package.
The command function §5's fourth rule waits on. Until one exists, the fourth rule cannot be written and RFC-2026-017 §3's present tense stays wrong, which RFC-2026-019's own status line already says.

A rule tying a blocker that names a decision record to that record's status, if one can be written without reading prose. Four manifests have now been corrected by hand for one class of defect, which is the point at which a control is usually cheaper than the next repair.
reviewer_instructions: Check the three removals against the artifacts, not against each other. The RFC-2026-018 one matters most: read that status line and confirm it now records the supersession, because the blocker called that shape the most dangerous one a record can have.
Check the three lint rules exist and assert what the blocker says they assert. Line numbers are given but the assertion is the thing to match.

Check that the untouched A1 blocker really is still true -- grep evidence/ for a review whose subject is RFC-2026-019 and confirm the countersignature that exists is about RFC-2026-016 and RFC-2026-017.
Confirm the status is still in_progress and nothing outside this package's two owned files changed.
